meta.title: The Parameterized Scheduling Zoo
meta.note: Seed dataset for prototyping the UI. Entries marked "confidence": "verified" reflect well-known landmark results; entries marked "illustrative" are plausible placeholders standing in for real results and should be checked against the literature before being trusted. Classical α|β|γ notation follows Graham, Lawler, Lenstra & Rinnooy Kan (1979).

complexityClasses.label: FPT
complexityClasses.description: Fixed-parameter tractable: solvable in f(k)·poly(n) time.

complexityClasses.label: XP
complexityClasses.description: Solvable in n^f(k) time; not known to be FPT.

complexityClasses.label: W[1]-hard
complexityClasses.description: W[1]-hard: unlikely to be FPT under standard assumptions.

complexityClasses.label: W[2]-hard
complexityClasses.description: W[2]-hard: unlikely to be FPT (stronger than W[1]).

complexityClasses.label: para-NP-hard
complexityClasses.description: NP-hard even for a constant value of the parameter.

complexityClasses.label: open
complexityClasses.description: Complexity status not known / not settled.

parameters.name: vertex cover number of the precedence graph

problems.name: Single machine, makespan
problems.classicalStatus: Trivially polynomial (schedule all jobs back to back in any order).

results.reference: Lenstra 1983 (ILP in fixed dimension); Mnich & Wiese, Math. Programming 2015
results.note: Encode as an ILP whose number of variables depends only on m; solvable in f(m)·poly(n) time via Lenstra's algorithm.
The classic O(n·m·p_max) subset-sum-style DP is already FPT when p_max is the parameter.

results.reference: cf. Knop & Koutecký, IPCO 2018 (n-fold IP techniques)
results.note: Group jobs by processing time and use an n-fold integer programming formulation of dimension depending on #p and m.
Placeholder — not meaningful for identical machines; included to show how an 'open' cell renders.

problems.name: Unrelated machines, makespan
problems.classicalStatus: NP-hard (strongly); 2-approximable. Lenstra, Shmoys & Tardos, Math. Programming 1990.

results.note: FPT via Lenstra-type ILP algorithm, parameter m bounds the number of integer variables.

results.reference: listed as an open direction in Mnich & van Bevern, Computers & OR 2018
results.note: Whether the problem is FPT in p_max alone is not settled in this seed dataset.
Same ILP-in-fixed-dimension argument as P||Cmax, generalized to machine speeds.
Group machines by speed class; n-fold IP dimension depends on #speeds and m.

problems.name: Identical machines with precedence constraints, makespan
problems.classicalStatus: NP-hard for general m (Garey & Johnson 1979); already hard for m=2 with arbitrary processing times (Ullman 1975).

results.reference: Bodlaender & Fellows, Operations Research Letters 1995 — “W[2]-hardness of precedence constrained k-processor scheduling”
results.note: Landmark hardness result: adding precedence constraints pushes the m-parameterization from FPT (unrelated/identical machines without precedence) to W[2]-hard.

results.reference: cf. dynamic programming over tree decompositions (Bodlaender-style), needs verification
results.note: Bounded-treewidth precedence DAGs admit a DP that tracks a bounded-size frontier of the decomposition.

problems.name: Single machine, release dates, total completion time
problems.classicalStatus: NP-hard (strongly). Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker, Ann. Discrete Math. 1977.

results.reference: cf. Hermelin et al.—style “number of distinct X” parameterizations; needs verification
results.note: Jobs sharing a release date form interchangeable blocks; state space depends only on #distinct release dates.

problems.name: Single machine, weighted number of tardy jobs

results.reference: cf. Hermelin, Karhi, Pinedo & Shabtay-style results on distinct-weight parameterizations; needs verification
results.note: With few distinct weight classes, an ILP/DP of dimension depending on #w becomes tractable.
Solvable in n^f(#p) time via brute-force over per-class schedules; not known whether this can be improved to FPT.
